_readme: The demo's save point, and the whole of the save-at-a-point half of GameConfig.save_policy.
A choice carrying `open_save`, which is the counter's idiom (`open_shop`) and the inn's
(`rest`): the runner collects, the world acts once the conversation has closed.
The wording is Dragon Quest's, whose King Lorik is the genre's first save point and whose
exact NES line is 'Will thou tell me now of thy deeds so they won't be forgotten?' followed
by 'Thy deeds have been recorded on the Imperial Scrolls of Honor.' The archaic register is
not borrowed - a template's demo should not read as somebody else's game - but the SHAPE is:
a person asks, the player answers, and the recording is spoken of as a thing that lasts.
He heals NOTHING, and that is researched rather than assumed. Every free save point in the
references restores nothing at all - Dragon Quest's king, Dragon Quest IV's church, Chrono
Trigger's save points, EarthBound's telephone. The one that heals fully is Final Fantasy I's
INN, which is a paid rest that happens to also save. This village already has that inn, and
it charges four gold; a free full heal standing beside it would make the innkeeper a mistake.
Both replies END the talk, the choice-line rule: cancel cannot escape a choice, so a
conversation that looped back through one would have no way out.
He says nothing about HAVING saved, because he cannot: the effects of a conversation are
applied when it CLOSES, so the slot list opens after his last word. The screen does the
announcing - the row the player is pointing at changes to say what it now holds, which is
the reference games' rule too (every one of the six tells you the save happened).

greet.speaker: Chronicler
greet.text:
Roads eat travellers, and the village
forgets them by spring.

ask.speaker: Chronicler
ask.text:
Shall I set your journey down,
so far as it has gone?

written.speaker: Chronicler
written.text: Then hold still. Ink is slow.

later.speaker: Chronicler
later.text:
The page keeps. Come back
before the road does.
